SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.

4. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

8. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

9. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

10. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.

13. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

14. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

15. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Light.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
